chapters.title: Explore the upper limb.
chapters.prompt: Rotate the upper limb to the right a full 360 degrees.

chapters.title: Locate the shoulder girdle.
chapters.prompt: Based on the notes, click on the bones that make up the shoulder girdle.

chapters.title: Locate the only horizontal long bone in the body.
chapters.prompt: The clavicle is the only horizontal long bone found in the body. Locate the clavicle.

chapters.title: Identify the anterior distal end of the humerus.
chapters.prompt: Rotate the model to find the anterior distal end of the humerus, then click on the correct location using the red cursor.

chapters.title: Locate the radius.
chapters.prompt: Locate the radius and click on the corresponding bone.

chapters.title: What is the mnemonic the we learned in class to help you remember the radius?
chapters.prompt: Check your notes if you can't remember!

chapters.title: Identify the carpal bones.
chapters.prompt: Use the hotspot tool to select one of the carpal bones.

chapters.title: Identify the most distal phalanx of the fingers.
chapters.prompt: To complete this activity find the most distal bone of the fingers.

chapters.title: Identify the misplaced bone.
chapters.prompt: This lesson involves bones of the appendicular skeleton (arms and legs). Identify the bone that does not belong to this skeleton, but rather belongs to the axial skeleton.
chapters.hint: Look at your notes on the axial versus appendicular skeleton!

chapters.title: Unique femur features.
chapters.prompt: Using your notes on the femur, please describe one unique feature of the femur.

chapters.title: Hip Replacement
chapters.prompt: Hip replacement is a common disorder involving the femur, where the proximal epiphysis of the femur is removed and replaced with a plastic or metal head. Locate the proximal epiphysis of the femur. CAUTION - you only have three attempts at this identification before the chapter resets!

chapters.title: Patella dislocation.
chapters.prompt: A soccer player makes a sharp turn on the field and feels a sudden "pop" in the front of their knee. They fall to the turf, unable to bear weight or straighten their leg, and notice a visible displacement on the side of their knee joint. At the clinic, the doctor diagnoses a dislocated patella.

chapters.title: Find the interosseous membrane.
chapters.prompt: The interosseous membrane is a fibrous sheet of connective tissue between the tibia and fibula that holds the two bones together. Locate this membrane.

chapters.title: Balance and the phalanges.
chapters.prompt:
A track athlete visits the clinic complaining of foot pain after a fall. They are having a hard time keeping their balance while standing still and struggle to push off the ground when sprinting.

An X-ray reveals an injury to a specific toe that is made up of only two bones: a proximal phalanx and a distal phalanx. Locate these two bones in the foot.
chapters.hint: Unlike the other four toes that each have three bones, this toe only has two! It plays a huge role in keeping you upright, and losing it severely impacts your balance when you walk or run.

chapters.title: A basketball player sustains an injury.
chapters.prompt:
A basketball player lands awkwardly after going up for a rebound and immediately feels sharp pain in the back of their foot. The athletic trainer notices they can't put weight down when taking a step, especially during the initial ground-impact phase of walking.

An X-ray confirms a stress fracture in the calcaneus.
